```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(plotly)
```

## The question

Do heavier, more powerful cars use more fuel?

- Data: `mtcars` (32 car models, built into R)
- Tool: Plotly (drag to rotate, scroll to zoom, hover for car names)
- Created on `r format(Sys.Date(), '%B %d, %Y')`

<style>
.reveal .controls{color:#e8590c!important;font-size:24px!important}
.reveal .controls .controls-arrow{animation:pulse 1.2s ease-in-out infinite}
@keyframes pulse{0%,100%{opacity:1}50%{opacity:.25}}
</style>

## Interactive 3D plot

```{r plot1}
mtcars$cyl_f <- factor(mtcars$cyl, labels = c("4 cyl", "6 cyl", "8 cyl"))
mtcars$car <- rownames(mtcars)

plot_ly(mtcars, x = ~wt, y = ~hp, z = ~mpg, color = ~cyl_f,
        colors = c("#2b8a3e", "#f59f00", "#e03131"),
        type = "scatter3d", mode = "markers",
        marker = list(size = 6, opacity = 0.9),
        text = ~car, hoverinfo = "text+x+y+z") %>%
  layout(scene = list(
           xaxis = list(title = "Weight (1000 lbs)"),
           yaxis = list(title = "Horsepower"),
           zaxis = list(title = "Miles per gallon")),
         legend = list(title = list(text = "Cylinders")))
```

## Takeaway

- Heavier cars get fewer miles per gallon
- More horsepower also means fewer miles per gallon
- 8-cylinder cars sit in the heavy, powerful, thirsty corner
